newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan gets $1 bln foreign investment in '95/96.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan gets $1 bln foreign investment in '95/96.

text.p: Pakistan received $1.1 billion in direct foreign investment in 1995/96 (July-June), up from $442 million in 1994/95, a government official said on Tuesday.

Mohibullah Shah, secretary at the state-run Board of Investment (BOI), told a news conference that 30 percent of the funds had gone to the energy sector while the rest had been invested in transport, communications and agriculture.

Shah said portfolio investment in 1995/96 had plunged to about $250 million from $1.0 billion in 1994/95, when share offers by state-run Pakistan Telecommunication Corporation (PTC) had attracted interest in local and international markets.
PTC was converted into Pakistan Telecommunication Co Ltd on January 1. The government plans to sell a 26 percent stake and transfer management control to a strategic investor in 1996/97.
Shah said the United States had invested $319 million, Britain $317 million, Japan $50 million, the United Arab Emirates and Hong Kong $40 million in Pakistan in 1995/96.
He said Pakistan was becoming uncompetitive in the region and foreign investors were deterred by the high cost of capital due to inefficient banking and rising cost of utilities.
The withdrawal in January of concessions to investors in special industrial zones under pressure from the International Monetary Fund had also had a negative effect, he said.
Shah said he wanted the zones to be revived.
"Only in 11 months, before this package was withdrawn, Pakistan received projects worth $2.0 billion.

"If we want to bring foreign investment we will have to give investors special incentives, particularly when we lack infrastructure, have a poor labour force and the cost of capital and utilities is high," he said.
Shah said Pakistan was working hard to achieve annual foreign investment of about $5.0 billion by the year 2000.
